八音桶鼓於1978年由日本鼓廠推出，並由Billy Cobham代言。早期產品以: The octoban was brought out by a Japanese drum maker in 1978 and endorsed by Billy Cobham. The early models had fibreglass shells coated in black lacquer, and the hoop design gave the head the largest possible striking area. Between 1978 and 1984 there were eight-piece sets and four-piece high and low sets; in 1985 the shells were shortened, and the low set was discontinued because it was hard to move on stage. The name later became a general term for sets of narrow-diameter tube drums, and other makers produce them in various materials and diameters.
八音桶鼓的原製鼓身以玻璃纖維製成，外殼塗黑漆，內部可見淺褐色原色；另有壓克力鼓身: The original octoban shell is fibreglass, lacquered black on the outside with the pale brown natural colour visible inside; there are also acrylic shells, which damage more easily. Other makers use fibreglass, acrylic, aluminium or wood for the shell, and home builders use PVC pipe. The sounding body is a single-headed drum with a clear head, though the source does not say what the head is made of; the materials of the hoops, lugs and other parts are not given either.
八音桶鼓音色明亮且銳利，具有獨特的穿透力，能在樂隊中清晰凸顯。其音域偏高，跨越中: The octoban's timbre is bright and sharp, with a penetration of its own that lets it stand out clearly in a band. Its range lies high, across the middle and upper register, and each drum has a different pitch, which gives a melodic effect. Because the shell is deep and the diameter small, the sound is relatively clean and compact and the resonance short, so each stroke comes out clearly separated. Next to a tom, the octoban is sharper and brighter; next to a conga, it lacks warmth of resonance. Its particular membranophone character gives it a bell-like metallic quality, most obvious in the upper register. It is exactly this bright timbre that makes the octoban an important part of the modern drum kit for visual and aural effect.
八音桶鼓（Octoban，又稱管狀桶鼓）是深筒、小口徑、單面鼓皮的膜鳴桶鼓，以鼓: The octoban (also called tube tom) is a membranophone drum with a deep shell, a small diameter and a single head, struck with drumsticks; it was originally tuned melodically as a set of eight, and the name comes from 'octo' and octave. It is usually added to a kit as one, two or four drums, mounted either as a square cluster of four or in a straight line on a stand. A Japanese maker introduced it in 1978; Billy Cobham endorsed it, and Stewart Copeland used the low set.

坐或站，將鼓置於身前合適位置。將鼓穩定放置於地面或夾於雙腿之間。用手掌或鼓棒敲擊: Sit or stand and put the drum in a suitable position in front of you. Set the drum firmly on the ground or hold it between the legs. Strike the centre or the edge of the head with the palm or a stick; different positions give different tones. The force of the stroke sets the volume. The sound is made by striking, so watch the position and the force.
